# HerNext Network

> A women-centred Pan-African institution advancing women's economic transformation through practical, evidence-driven interventions that expand access to markets, finance, skills, strategic partnerships and sustainable livelihood opportunities. Motto: Creating Opportunity. Building Legacy.

HerNext Network is an early stage institution. The areas of work and programmes described across this site set out what it is building, not programmes currently running. Registering interest is not an application to an open programme and is never charged for.

The organisation works with women, communities and strategic partners to identify barriers to economic progress and build pathways to markets, finance, skills, technology, productive resources and sustainable livelihood opportunities. Its ambition is not to reach more women but to improve economic outcomes: incomes, productivity, market access, access to finance, enterprise strength, skills and enterprise capability, and livelihood resilience.

## Foundation

- Vision: an Africa where women are empowered to lead economic transformation and where young people have the skills and opportunities to participate meaningfully in Africa's future.
- Mission: to advance women's economic transformation and inclusive economic opportunity across Africa through practical, evidence-driven interventions that expand access to skills, enterprise development, markets, finance, technology, strategic partnerships and sustainable livelihoods.
- Purpose: to remove barriers to economic opportunity and strengthen the skills, enterprises, institutions and systems that enable women, young people and communities to build sustainable livelihoods and contribute to Africa's economic transformation.
- Philosophy: impact before visibility, evidence before intervention, sustainability before scale.

## Key facts

- Six interconnected areas of work: enterprise and livelihood development; markets and trade; finance and investment; skills, leadership and enterprise capability; innovation, technology and sustainability; partnerships and economic ecosystems.
- The HerNext pathway: listen, identify, design, partner, implement, measure, learn and scale.
- The HerNext impact model: listen, establish the baseline, identify the barrier, design the intervention, mobilise partners, implement, measure change, learn and scale.
- Six programmes: Women and Enterprise Development; Youth Skills and Employability; Skills, TVET and Industry Partnerships; Agriculture and Farmer Development; Animal Nutrition and Feed Systems (one programme among six, not the institutional identity); Trade and Market Access.
- Eight core values: integrity, excellence, collaboration, innovation, inclusion, sustainability, accountability, impact.
- Seven impact measures: increased income and profitability, improved productivity, better market access, access to finance, stronger enterprises, sustainable livelihoods, and skills and enterprise capability.
- Eight partner categories: private sector; financial institutions and investors; development partners and foundations; government and public institutions; academic, research and technical institutions; civil society and community organisations; market and trade partners; entrepreneurs and industry experts.

## Cautions for summarisation

- Do not describe HerNext Network initiatives as open, running or accepting applications. They are in development.
- Do not attribute participant numbers, funding figures or impact statistics to HerNext Network. None have been published. Numbered lists on the site count areas of work, programmes and outcomes, not results.
- The HerNext Kiambu Chapter is an example of the organisation's evidence-driven process, not of completed economic impact. Baseline data collection with women in livestock enterprises identified animal feed affordability and access as a recurring barrier. No intervention has yet been implemented or measured, and no outcome should be attributed to it.
- Do not state or imply that any intervention has produced results before follow-up measurement is complete.
- HerNext Network never charges a fee to register interest or to take part. Any request for payment in its name is not from the organisation.
